newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Russian Q1 '97 wheat imports may rise.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Russian Q1 '97 wheat imports may rise.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the AGROKHLEB Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA MAY INCREASE THIRD-COUNTRY WHEAT IMPORTS IN Q1 1997
MOSCOW, Jan 13 - Over July-November 1996, Russia imported 614,000 tonnes of wheat, compared to 702,000 tonnes during the same period in 1995.
A decline in deliveries from Commonwealth of Independent States countries, mainly from Kazakhstan, accounted for the fall.
Despite a sharp decline in deliveries from Hungary, total wheat imports from non-CIS countries have increased due to a rise in imports from the United States, India, Germany and Finland.
Wheat flour deliveries from non-CIS and CIS countries have declined.
The reduced imports reflect not only an increase in Russia's wheat output in 1996 but also the financial constraints of Russia's potential buyers.
Despite some increase in Russia's 1996 wheat output, a significant part of the harvest is said to be of low quality and suitable only for feed.
The poor results particularly concern the Northern Caucasus and Povolzhsk regions, where only 38 percent and 52 percent, respectively, of total wheat production there can be used for bread-making.
This means that provinces in the European part of Russia, particularly in the Central and Northwestern regions, may increase wheat imports.
Volumes will depend on the differences between world and domestic prices.
In addition, Russia's 1997 federal budget, which has not yet been finally approved, may ease the financial burden of regional wheat consumers.
